title: Overturo consent record (overturo-cr/2.9)
description: The canonical record frozen at fulfillment, organized into the ISO/IEC TS 27560:2023 sections, in three kinds: consent records; notice records (notice-not-consent mechanisms and anonymous completions; Kantara ANCR Stage-1 aligned); and authorization records. The `extensions` member carries platform facts the standard has no slot for, per the standards' own non-conflicting-additions allowance. Renders add a render-time `receipt_metadata` section NOT described here: the frozen record never carries render state. The authorization_record kind is durable evidence of a delegated-authority commitment. Its `authority` section is 27560-ALIGNED structure, not PII-processing subject matter; conformance language applies only to records carrying a pii_processing section.

record.description: The record's identity: the schema version it follows, the standard it conforms to, the record identifier, the kind, and whether the record is anonymous.

record_id.description: The unique, stable identifier of this record — the receipt's identity across every channel and export flavor, and the record-specific identifier that stands in for the principal on anonymous records.

record_type.description: The receipt kind. notice_record covers notice-not-consent mechanisms (informed, documented) and anonymous completions; its event section carries notice events, never a consent-given event. Absent on records issued before this field existed: read as consent_record. authorization_record covers delegated-authority commitments: it requires the authority section, carries pii_processing exactly when declared purposes exist, and its event section uses authority states.

anonymous.description: Kantara ANCR Stage 1 — emitted (true only) when the subject completed without an established identity. The record-specific identifier standing in for the principal is record_id itself; pii_principal_id is FORBIDDEN below.

pii_principal_id.description: The principal reference. Required for identified records; forbidden for anonymous ones (the conditional below validates the rule — anonymity is enforced, not conventioned).

pii_processing.description: The granted purposes with their decision-time facts: language and jurisdiction, the notice as presented, the collection method, each purpose's lawful basis, categories, retention, storage and recipients, and how consent is withdrawn.

language.description: The language the decision was presented in (locale code). Frozen labels throughout the record are in this language.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction governing this processing, as configured by the organization; "unspecified" when none is declared.

privacy_notice.description: The VERSIONED notice reference (ISO/IEC TS 27560 clause 6.3.4.2/clause 6.2.2.6): the notice as presented, content-addressed. The hashed content set is exactly {locale, presentation title+description, policy_url, flow-visible purpose rows (name/label/description/mechanism/required, sorted by name)} — canonical deep-sorted JSON, sha256; growing the set is a schema minor, never silent. Three shapes coexist: locally-authored records always carry reference+hash (+url when the organization declared a policy URL); cross-region records carry what the authoring region's offer sent; records upgraded from the earlier flat shape carry url only (nothing is fabricated). Absent only for cross-region offers that predate this field and declared no policy URL.

hash.description: sha256:<hex> over the canonical content set.

url.description: The organization's declared privacy policy URL, when one exists.

collection_method.description: How the decision was collected, as shown to the subject (ISO/IEC TS 27560 clause 6.3.4.9) — the human-readable form of extensions.collection_mechanism.

purpose.description: The purpose label exactly as presented to the subject at decision time, in the record's language.

purpose_id.description: The stable machine identifier of the purpose (also the key scoped withdrawal events reference).

description.description: The purpose description as presented at decision time, when the organization declared one.

lawful_basis.description: The lawful basis for this purpose (ISO/IEC TS 27560 clause 6.3.4.7), as a human-readable label frozen at decision time.

consent_mechanism.description: How consent for this purpose was collected, as a human-readable label — one flow can mix mechanisms per purpose.

pii_category.description: Human-readable categories of the personal data this purpose covers (ISO/IEC TS 27560 clause 6.3.4.10) — the display projection of pii_information.

retention_period.description: ISO 8601 duration from the purpose's declared retention period (27560 6.3.4.13); honest-absent when the purpose declares none.

purpose_type.description: The canonical purpose-taxonomy domain (27560 6.3.4.6); honest-absent for custom purposes outside the taxonomy.

pii_information.description: Structured attributes (27560 Table 3) — the source data behind pii_category (one derivation feeds both; no divergence possible). Per-attribute sensitive/special flags are documented-absent in v1.

pii_type.description: Human-readable name of the personal-data attribute.

pii_attribute_id.description: The stable machine identifier of the attribute (the platform permission name).

pii_optional.description: Whether the subject could complete the decision without granting this attribute.

purposes.description: The GRANTED purposes only, with their decision-time labels frozen (ISO/IEC TS 27560 clause 6.3.4.5). Purposes declined or later revoked do not appear here; revocations appear in the event lifecycle and the render-time status.

storage_locations.description: Where the data is stored (ISO country codes) — derived from the platform's residency rules (where the subject's data lives), never declared by hand.

processing_locations.description: Present only when recorded lawful-transfer bases exist for the flow: their destination jurisdictions. Absent means no recorded cross-border processing.

withdrawal_method.description: The stable, credential-free entry point for withdrawing consent (27560 6.3.4.19). Never a minted access token: tokens expire, receipts do not.

recipient_third_parties.description: Party ids of third-party recipients (each has a corresponding party_identification row — 27560 6.3.4.18). An EMPTY array asserts nothing is shared; an ABSENT key means the platform cannot enumerate recipients completely (e.g. externally-configured webhooks) and stays silent rather than implying completeness.

privacy_rights.description: Where the subject exercises their rights (27560 6.3.4.20): the stable access entry and, for full accounts, the self-service export. String encoding per the standard; labels live in the rendering layer.

processing_method.description: How the PII is processed (27560 6.3.4.11): the ENFORCED capability identifiers from the activation-frozen composition snapshot (signed with the flow). Identifiers only, never configuration. Absent for flows without a composition.

impact_assessment.description: Reference to the organization's completed legitimate-interest assessment (27560 6.3.4.22), emitted only when a granted purpose runs on legitimate interest and exactly one active assessment exists.

party_identification.description: The controller (declared legal identity when the org completed its controller identity record — provenance 'declared'; display-name fallback otherwise), the platform processor row, and the catalogued supervisory authority. Identity data is DECLARED by the organization, never verified by the platform. party_role values in use: controller, processor, supervisory_authority (string-typed — later members may add roles).

party_id.description: The party's stable public identifier — for the controller, the application identifier the transparency record is keyed by; for recipients, the pointer recipient_third_parties references.

party_name.description: The party's name: the declared legal name where an identity record exists (provenance "declared"), else the display name.

party_role.description: The party's role in this processing: controller, processor, supervisory_authority, recipient - or, on authorization records, principal (a co-signing grantor) and agent (the authorized software agent).

party_type.description: Whether the party is an organization, a natural person, or a software_agent. Persons are never emitted as recipients.

street_address.description: Street address line of the party's declared postal address.

locality.description: City or locality of the declared postal address.

region.description: State, province, or region line of the declared postal address.

postal_code.description: Postal code of the declared postal address.

country.description: Country of the declared postal address (ISO country code).

party_email.description: The party's declared contact email for privacy matters (ISO/IEC TS 27560 clause 6.3.6; the Kantara CR v1.1 required contact).

party_phone.description: The party's declared contact phone for privacy matters.

party_url.description: The party's declared contact or informational URL.

authority.description: Authorization records only. States the enforced grant verbatim: each bound dimension appears exactly when the platform enforces it - absence means not configured, never 'unlimited'. Bound-dimension inner shapes are owned by the platform's authority-bounds vocabulary; this schema constrains presence, not structure.

scope_bounds.description: Which data scopes the agent may access or share (allowed/denied lists), as enforced.

action_bounds.description: Which operations the agent may perform (allowed/denied verb lists), as enforced.

value_bounds.description: Financial ceilings — per transaction and cumulative, with currency — as enforced.

time_bounds.description: The operating window (active days/hours) and hard expiry, as enforced.

escalation_bounds.description: Thresholds that force the agent to defer to its principal (approval triggers), as enforced.

reputation_bounds.description: Minimum counterparty trust requirements the agent must respect, as enforced.

jurisdiction_bounds.description: The jurisdictions the agent may act toward, as enforced at authorization time.

sequence_bounds.description: The eighth enforced dimension, carried on its own grant column; present only when configured.

valid_from.description: The declared start of the authority (ISO 8601).

valid_until.description: The declared end of the authority (ISO 8601); absent for open-ended grants.

cooling_off.description: ISO 8601 duration between commitment and activation; present only when an activation delay existed.

withdrawal_method.description: Stable revocation entry URL; never embeds a credential - the principal authenticates on arrival.

event.description: The lifecycle as a projection of the platform's existing evidence (tamper-evident audit-trail records, transaction timestamps) — never a new event store. Consent records freeze the pre-decision prefix (notice shown, consent requested) plus the given event, in canonical lifecycle order; notice records freeze notice vocabulary instead — see event_state. Renders append post-decision transitions (withdrawn — optionally scoped by purpose_id — and expired) derived at read time. Arrays are heterogeneous by construction: flows whose delivery path does not record an opening start at "consent requested"; records issued before the lifecycle section existed start at "consent given"; system-mediated records are notice records carrying the single constructive "notice shown". "consent refused" is defined but unissued in v1 (records exist only for completed decisions; refusal evidence belongs to the notice-receipt track). States "consent invalidated" and "consent halted" remain reserved: no platform transition claims them yet. Actor attribution: the principal for given/withdrawn/acknowledged (anonymous records substitute record_id); the controller (application) for notice shown/requested; the platform processor for expiry. Authorization records: the frozen prefix carries 'authority requested' and 'authority granted'; renders append the lifecycle derived from existing evidence (the grant's chronicle trail, the receipt-consumption aggregate) — 'authority exercised' rows are AGGREGATES (see occurrences), suspension/resumption pairs are dated history, approvals carry the human decision with real attribution, and 'authority expired' is suppressed after a revocation. Records frozen before lifecycle events were recorded start at 'authority granted' (frozen means frozen). Histories without audit-trail records emit only what their columns can date.

event_time.description: When the event occurred (ISO 8601). Times come from platform evidence — never synthesized.

validity_duration.description: ISO 8601 duration (exact, second precision), present only when the consent carries an expiry.

entity_id.description: Who acted: the principal reference for given/withdrawn/acknowledged (anonymous records substitute record_id), the application for notice shown/requested, the platform processor for expiry.

event_state.description: Notice records map evidence to notice vocabulary: interactive flows carry notice shown (from the display evidence) + notice acknowledged (completion, entity = principal or, for anonymous records, record_id); system/documented records carry a single constructive notice shown (entity = the application) and no acknowledged row. Notice records never carry consent given.

purpose_id.description: Present only on a scoped withdrawal: the withdrawn purpose's purpose_id (matches pii_processing.purposes[].purpose_id). Absent on record-level events.

record_reference.description: Re-affirmation linkage (Annex B re-confirm): on a given event, the record_id of the predecessor record this consent supersedes. The predecessor's render carries the inverse reference in receipt_metadata (render state, not frozen).

occurrences.description: Aggregate rows only (authority exercised): the authority was exercised this many times, most recently at event_time. Never present on single-occurrence events.

approval_id.description: Approval-scoped rows: the public reference of the human decision, matching the oversight evidence package's rows. Requested rows may lack it (the reference exists only once the decision row does).

extensions.description: Documented platform extensions (Kantara CR v1.1 clause 4.2; ISO/IEC TS 27560 clause 6.3.2.2): facts the standard has no slot for. Every key is documented here; nothing standard-named carries non-standard semantics.

collection_mechanism.description: The raw platform consent-mechanism value; pii_processing.collection_method carries the human label.

delivery_mode.description: How the decision surface was delivered: redirect, embed, popup, or link.

scopes.description: The effective granted platform permissions at fulfillment — operational grant state, distinct from the purpose grants above.

sensitive.description: True when the flow collected at least one field the organization classified at a sensitive level.

consent_flow_id.description: The stable public identifier of the flow (the versioned notice reference is rooted in it).

grant_integrity.description: Authorization records only: the reference to the grant's dual signature - content hash + key versions. The signatures themselves are the signed-export payload, never inlined here.

canonical_hash.description: Content hash of the committed grant, computed at attestation time.

principal_key_version.description: Key version of the principal-side signature the hash was signed under.

platform_key_version.description: Key version of the platform-side signature the hash was signed under.

delegation_chain_root.description: Authorization records only: the root commitment's record reference when this authority was sub-delegated. Absent for root grants.

capability_manifest.description: Authorization records only: the capability-manifest version the grant was made against — the agent's declaration, content-addressed. The hashed content set is exactly {agent_type, name, delegated_scopes (sorted), and the operator-declared disclosure metadata: capabilities, operator_name, privacy_policy_url, data_storage, retention_period} — canonical deep-sorted JSON, sha256; growing the set is a schema minor, never silent. agent_type/name/delegated_scopes are platform-attested registration facts; the metadata keys are operator-DECLARED (the hash anchors what was declared, not that it is true). A model/version fingerprint has no substrate field today and is documented-absent from the set. Manifest drift is AGENT-side (what the agent declares); composition drift is FLOW-side (what a flow executes) — separate mechanisms, never conflated. Absent on records frozen before manifest pinning existed and when no unique agent resolves. Pinned at freeze; supersession never rewrites it (renders overlay manifest_superseded instead).

reference.description: The versioned natural-key reference ("<agent_id>/manifest/v<n>") resolvable at the published manifests route under the agent's transparency record.

hash.description: sha256 content hash ("sha256:<hex>") of the canonical deep-sorted declaration set — recompute over the published version content to verify.

accountability_record.description: Structural slot: the agent accountability record reference in effect at activation. Documented-absent until that member ships.

agent_disclosures.description: Consent and notice records only: the AI agents disclosed to the human this record belongs to — one entry per agent, EU AI Act Art. 50 aligned. A disclosure entry proves NOTICE (the human was told), never grant or authority: the commitment story lives in authorization records, and this array is schema-forbidden there. Present exactly when the flow disclosed agents (platform provenance) or the operator declared an out-of-band disclosure (declared provenance). Carries agent-side references only — never the counterparty's identity (the anonymous kind stays anonymous through these fields).

accountability_record.description: The agent's accountability record URL — 'operated by X' is resolvable, not just asserted, including after revocation (revocation never un-publishes).

capability_manifest.description: The capability-manifest version anchoring what the human was told about the agent — the disclosure card renders exactly the manifest's content set, so the manifest hash IS the disclosure-content hash (one content-address discipline, not a third). Optional: absent when no manifest applies, never fabricated.

reference.description: The versioned natural-key reference resolvable at the published manifests route.

hash.description: sha256 content hash of the canonical declaration set — recompute over the published version content to verify.

delivery_provenance.description: How the disclosure reached the human. 'platform': it rode a surface the platform itself rendered (the flow's agent-disclosure card) — the platform states it showed this. 'declared': the OPERATOR declared an out-of-band disclosure via API — the platform records the declaration and never certifies what it did not deliver (the declared posture: recorded, never certified). The two are never blurred; the API path cannot produce 'platform'.

disclosed_at.description: When the disclosure happened: the fulfillment moment on the platform path; the operator's declared timestamp on the declared path.

signature_evidence.description: Signing-party verification evidence: one entry per completed evidence envelope anchored to the signing party, sorted by completed_at. Pointer + digest only — verdict/claim CONTENT lives in the agreement export and evidence packages, never here. Present on consent records only, and only when the signing party's transaction carries completed evidence; honest-absent otherwise.

scheme.description: The evidence scheme: qualified_signature (a legally-recognized signature leg), role_verification (a verified organizational role), or verified_presentation (a verified digital credential).

method.description: The verification method that produced the evidence, one per scheme.

provider.description: The provider that produced the evidence.

status.description: Only completed evidence is referenced; pending or failed evidence never appears.

evidence_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical (deep-sorted JSON) evidence for this envelope — a content pointer, never the content. FREEZE-TIME-SCOPED: a point-in-time pointer computed when this record was frozen, not a live recompute target. Evidence stamped onto the envelope AFTER completion (e.g. a later revocation notice) is separate and does not retroactively change this digest; recomputing over the live envelope may therefore differ, by design.

completed_at.description: When the evidence completed (ISO 8601); the entries are sorted ascending by this value.
